info.name: COMP3123 Assignment 1 - 101496484
info.description:
COMP 3123 Assignment 1 - Secure REST API (Cem Dudu, 101496484).

How to run:
1. Start MongoDB and the API (npm start). Use an empty comp3123_assignment1 database.
2. Run the whole collection in order with the Collection Runner (folders 0 to 8).
3. Restart the server before running it again (rate-limit counters are kept in memory) and use an empty database (users alice and bob are created by folder 1).

Sample test users: alice / alice@example.com / AlicePass123 and bob / bob@example.com / BobPass123

Tokens and ids are saved in the collection variables by the test scripts (tokenA, tokenB, empA1_id, ...). Their initial values are empty, so no real token is stored in this file.

Manual tests: 5.4-5.5 (expired JWT, needs JWT_EXPIRES_IN=30s) and folder 8 (MongoDB stopped, 500). They are skipped in a normal run.

item.name: 5. JWT Authentication Errors
item.description: Requests to a protected route with a missing, invalid, tampered or expired token. All must return 401.

exec: pm.test("Error response is JSON with status false", () => pm.expect(json.status).to.eql(false));
pm.test("Message: No token provided", () => pm.expect(json.message).to.include("No token provided"));
pm.test("Error response is JSON with status false", () => pm.expect(json.status).to.eql(false));
// Change the user id inside User A's token to User B's id (signature stays the same)
pm.test("Error response is JSON with status false", () => pm.expect(json.status).to.eql(false));

request.description: Takes User A's real token and changes the user id inside it to User B's id, without a new signature. The signature check fails, so the server rejects it.
To test an expired token: start the server with JWT_EXPIRES_IN=30s, send this request, then send 5.5 (it waits until the token has expired). With the normal 1h setting, 5.5 is skipped.

item.name: 7. Rate Limiting (run last)
item.description: Login and signup share a limit of 20 requests per 15 minutes per IP (AUTH_RATE_LIMIT). In the Collection Runner, request 7.1 repeats itself until the server answers 429. Restart the server to reset the counters.

item.name: 7.1 Login - repeat until 429 Too Many Requests

exec: // The Collection Runner sends this request again until the server answers 429
pm.test("Status code is 429 Too Many Requests (attempt " + attempts + " in this run)", () => pm.response.to.have.status(429));
pm.test("Retry-After header tells the client when to try again", () => pm.response.to.have.header("Retry-After"));
pm.test("JSON error message is returned", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.include("Too many requests"));
pm.test("Attempt " + attempts + ": not limited yet (status " + pm.response.code + ")", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 401]));

item.name: 8. Manual Tests - Database Stopped (500)
item.description: Manual: stop MongoDB (for example "docker stop comp3123-mongo"), then send these requests. With MongoDB running, 8.1 is skipped and 8.2 only checks the normal health response.

exec: pm.test("Status code is 500 Internal Server Error", () => pm.response.to.have.status(500));
pm.test("Internal details are hidden from the client", () => pm.expect(json.message).to.eql("Internal server error"));
pm.test.skip("MongoDB is running - stop it to see the 500 response", () => {});

request.description: When MongoDB is stopped, the database call fails. The central error handler logs the full error and returns a general 500 message without internal details.

exec: pm.test("Health check reports the database status (" + json.database + ")", () => pm.expect(json.database).to.be.oneOf(["connected", "disconnected"]));
